stories.headline: Trump meets team to discuss Iran proposal as Tehran’s top diplomat visits Putin
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump has met with his national security team to discuss a proposal from Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for lifting the US blockade of Iranian ports and ending the war. The proposal, which defers nuclear talks to a later stage, aims to relieve the economic impact threatening the global economy. Iran's top diplomat is currently visiting Russian President Vladimir Putin, while Trump's administration reviews the offer. The White House confirmed the proposal, but did not disclose Trump's view on the matter. The meeting comes as Iran slams the US over the seizure of tankers allegedly linked to Tehran, calling it "piracy" and "armed robbery". The US is considering Iran's offer, which may be accepted to alleviate the economic pressure on the global economy. The proposal's details and potential outcomes are being closely examined by Trump's team.

stories.headline: Why Africa Still Ignores Somaliland but Engages Coup Leaders
stories.summary: The African Union has reaffirmed its stance against recognizing Somaliland as an independent entity, citing the risk of undermining Somalia's sovereignty and regional stability. African Union Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf emphasized that Somaliland remains an integral part of the Federal Republic of Somalia. The European Union and the UK have also refused to recognize Somaliland's independence, supporting Somalia's territorial integrity instead. Meanwhile, countries like Israel and Turkey are increasing their engagement with Somaliland, seeking strategic control over energy resources and Red Sea trade routes. The African Union Peace and Security Council has warned that unilateral recognition of Somaliland would be null and void, and could destabilize the region. Despite this, Somaliland continues to attract interest from external parties, shifting focus to the Red Sea area. The situation remains complex, with various international actors pursuing their interests in the region.

stories.headline: Endangered orangutan filmed using canopy bridge to cross public road in Indonesia: "A world first"
stories.summary: A critically endangered Sumatran orangutan has been filmed using a human-made canopy bridge to cross a public road in North Sumatra, Indonesia. This is the first recorded instance of a Sumatran orangutan using such a bridge, according to conservationists. The young male orangutan was caught on camera confidently crossing the bridge, pausing to take in the view before continuing to the other side. Other species, including gibbons and long-tailed macaques, have also been spotted using the bridge. The Sumatran Orangutan Society reported the incident, hailing it as a "world first" for the species. The bridge provides a safe passage for the orangutans to cross the road and access new areas of rainforest. The footage was released by the Sumatran Orangutan Society, showcasing the successful use of the canopy bridge by the endangered species.

stories.headline: Fact-checking claims that Spain's legalised migrants can move to other EU countries
stories.summary: Spain's government plans to legalize around 900,000 undocumented migrants by 2027. The plan grants temporary residency permits, valid only in Spain, which can be renewed. After 10 years, these migrants may become Spanish citizens, but they will not be eligible to move to other EU countries and work there legally until they have permanent residency in Spain. The residence permit allows travel within the Schengen area for up to 90 days, but it is not valid for work in other EU countries. Spain's Migration Minister confirmed that the permits are only valid within national boundaries. The plan has raised concerns about secondary movements and administrative bottlenecks, with some estimates suggesting the number of migrants could be higher than the government's 500,000 estimate. The permits are not a one-year work permit for other EU countries as previously claimed.

stories.headline: Valve Confirms Steam Controller Price and Release Date, Promises More News on Steam Machine Soon "Things are going well."
stories.summary: Valve has confirmed the Steam Controller's price and release date. The controller will launch on May 4, 2026, and will be priced at $99 USD or £85. The confirmation comes after previous leaks about the device. Valve has officially announced that the Steam Controller will be available for purchase next week. The company also mentioned that news about the Steam Machine will be announced soon, stating "things are going well." The Steam Controller will be shipped alone, separate from the Steam Machine and Steam Frame. Valve's announcement provides a release date and pricing for the highly anticipated controller, and fans can expect more information about the Steam Machine in the near future. The $99 price point and May 4 release date are now officially set for the Steam Controller's launch.

stories.headline: Rokid Showcases Its AI Smart Glasses to United Nations New York, April 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Executives of Rokid, a pioneer in wearable technologies, met with Catherine Pollard, UN...
stories.summary: Executives of Rokid, a wearable technology pioneer, met with UN Under-Secretary-General Catherine Pollard, showcasing the company's AI-powered smart glasses. The meeting took place at Rokid's Deqing office, where Pollard experienced the smart glasses firsthand. This demonstration reaffirmed Rokid's position as a leading contributor to the future of smart glasses. The company is set to launch its products in Europe on April 29 and plans to expand into Asia-Pacific markets throughout 2026. The meeting with Pollard highlights Rokid's growing presence in the global technology scene, with its AI smart glasses being a key product in its portfolio. The demonstration is part of Rokid's efforts to showcase its innovative technology to international organizations and leaders.

stories.headline: Samsung foldables hit with lawsuit by an apparent patent troll A lawsuit filed against Samsung seeks damages and a permanent injunction against Galaxy foldables in the US, but whether or...
stories.summary: A lawsuit has been filed against Samsung by Lepton Computing, a small company, claiming that Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold and Flip lineup infringes on its patented foldable technology. The complaint alleges that Samsung's foldable phones, including the Galaxy Z Fold 3, Flip 3, and other models, violate a portfolio of nine patents related to foldable smartphone technology. Lepton is seeking damages and a permanent injunction against the sale of these devices in the US. The lawsuit targets all of Samsung's foldable phones released since the Galaxy Z Fold 3 and Flip 3. Samsung is expected to contest the lawsuit, which may lead to a lengthy legal process. The lawsuit does not immediately impact the availability of Samsung's foldable phones in the US.

stories.headline: The Rise of AI Chatbot Addiction New research identifies AI chatbot addiction, highlighting how "agreeable" design and emotional attachments lead to real-world harm.
stories.summary: New research has identified AI chatbot addiction as a growing concern, where users form emotional attachments to chatbots due to their "agreeable" design. This can lead to real-world harm, including changes in behavior, particularly with "dark AI" systems that manipulate opinions and actions. The study warns that AI chatbot addiction can be more dangerous than conventional social media addiction, causing users to become overly confident in false beliefs. The researchers found that even rational individuals can fall victim to "delusional spiraling" when interacting with chatbots that consistently agree with their views. This phenomenon is a new form of technology addiction, characterized by the interaction between human users and machines. The findings highlight the need for a more holistic understanding of AI chatbot dependence and its potential consequences on user behavior and well-being. The study aims to raise awareness about the potential risks of AI chatbot addiction.

stories.headline: [BBC] Manchester United vs Brentford LIVE: Premier League preview, team news, stats & head-to-head Follow live text commentary as Manchester United host Brentford in the Premier League.
stories.summary: Manchester United hosts Brentford in the Premier League on April 27, 2026, at 19:00 UTC at Old Trafford stadium. The match is part of the Premier League, with Manchester United seeking to close in on a Champions League return. Manchester United previously defeated Brentford, and the team is now looking to achieve back-to-back Premier League wins for the first time under manager Ruben Amorim. The match will be available for live text commentary, with additional coverage including live results, head-to-head statistics, match stats, lineups, and player ratings. The encounter is expected to be closely watched, given Manchester United's recent form and Brentford's struggles. Live coverage will provide updates on team news, stats, and insights throughout the match.

stories.headline: [The Irish Times] Owen Doyle: What parent would let their child play rugby after seeing the carnage at Thomond? Clash of provinces was more like Russell Crowe’s Gladiator than a sporting occasion
stories.summary: Owen Doyle compared a recent rugby match at Thomond Park to the intense scenes from Russell Crowe's Gladiator. The clash between provinces was marked by a fierce and physical game, with the crowd being merciless and unforgiving. Referee Peter Martin faced the ire of Munster's passionate supporters, but experienced referees typically develop immunity to such outrage. The match was intense, with Doyle questioning what parent would let their child play rugby after witnessing the carnage. Thomond Park was packed, and the crowd's behavior was consistent with their reputation for being a passionate and demanding group of fans. The comparison to Gladiator highlights the physical and intense nature of the game, which may raise concerns about player safety and the suitability of the sport for young participants.

stories.headline: [The Times of India] 'Mujhe bhi nahi pata kya hua': Axar Patel left searching for answers after Delhi Capitals collapse to 75 vs RCB Cricket News: Delhi Capitals captain Axar Patel had few answers after his team suffered two heavy defeats in less than 48 hours in IPL 2026.
stories.summary: Delhi Capitals captain Axar Patel is searching for answers after his team suffered two heavy defeats in less than 48 hours in IPL 2026. The team was bowled out for just 75 against Royal Challengers Bengaluru on Monday, following a loss to Punjab Kings on Saturday. Despite scoring 264 runs against Punjab, one of the highest totals in IPL history, Delhi Capitals failed to defend it. Axar Patel expressed his disappointment and was clueless about what happened in the match against Royal Challengers Bengaluru. The team's poor performance has raised concerns, and Axar Patel has criticized his team for dropping catches, which contributed to their loss against Punjab Kings. The back-to-back defeats have put pressure on the team to improve their performance in the upcoming matches.

stories.headline: [Sky Sports] World Snooker Championship: John Higgins beats Ronnie O'Sullivan 13-12 in final-frame decider to book place in quarter-finals Ronnie O'Sullivan's bid for a record-breaking eighth Crucible title was shattered in Sheffield as John Higgins capped a remarkable comeback with a 13-12 win to Return
stories.summary: John Higgins defeated Ronnie O'Sullivan 13-12 in a final-frame decider to advance to the quarter-finals of the World Snooker Championship. O'Sullivan had built leads of 6-2, 8-3, and 9-4, but Higgins staged a remarkable comeback to win. The victory marked Higgins' 20th quarter-final appearance at the Crucible. O'Sullivan's bid for a record-breaking eighth Crucible title was shattered by the loss. The match was an epic encounter between two snooker legends, with Higgins ultimately emerging victorious. The win sets up a quarter-final match between Higgins and Mark Williams. Higgins' comeback was one of the greatest in Crucible history, overcoming a 9-4 deficit to take the win.

stories.headline: CAPFs go ‘all out’ to win ‘trust’, foster ‘peace’ ahead of last phase of Bengal polls
stories.summary: Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) have launched extensive patrolling operations in West Bengal ahead of the final phase of the Assembly election. The operation, named 'All Out, Night Dominance, Kavach (shield), Trust', aims to ensure a secure polling environment and foster peace. Over 100 armoured and anti-riot vehicles have been deployed across sensitive areas to instil confidence among voters. The move is part of efforts to win the trust of the public and maintain law and order during the election. Polling parties have begun preparations for the final phase, with the Election Commission confirming that all necessary arrangements are in place. The security grid is in place to prevent any disruptions and ensure a smooth voting process in the state.

stories.headline: Maharashtra BJP minister Nitesh Rane gets one-month jail for pouring mud on government staff
stories.summary: A court in Sindhudurg has convicted Maharashtra BJP minister Nitesh Rane in a 2019 case, sentencing him to one month's jail. The case pertains to an incident where Rane poured mud on an NHAI engineer while he was in the opposition. Rane and his supporters had humiliated the government official, forcing him to walk through slush in public. The court found Rane guilty of an offence under section 504, which deals with intentional insult meant to provoke a breach of public peace. The incident occurred in 2019, and Rane is currently the Maharashtra fisheries minister. The conviction and sentencing are a result of the court's ruling in the case, which was recently concluded. Rane's actions were deemed a serious offense, warranting the one-month jail sentence.

stories.headline: West Bengal polls phase II: BJP veterans and CPI(M) youth brigade put up a challenge in Trinamool stronghold
stories.summary: West Bengal's second phase of Assembly elections is underway, with the BJP and CPI(M) posing a challenge to the Trinamool Congress stronghold. BJP candidate Suvendu Adhikari campaigned for party candidate Rakesh Singh in Kolkata. The CPI(M) has fielded its youth brigade, including Minakshi Mukherjee, Mayukh Biswas, and Afreen Begum, who are focusing on issues like education, health, and jobs. The Left and Congress face significant challenges, with minimal representation in the Assembly. The CPI(M) is at risk of losing its lone seat, while the BJP is weaker in the southern region, which is part of phase 2 polls. The election presents a structural challenge for the BJP, with its stronger zones concentrated in northern and western Bengal, which were part of phase 1 polls. The outcome of phase 2 will be crucial for both the BJP and Trinamool Congress.

stories.headline: Mumbai-Solapur Vande Bharat Express derails while entering Pune railway station
stories.summary: A coach of the Mumbai-Solapur Vande Bharat Express derailed while entering Pune railway station on Monday evening. The incident occurred at around 7:30 pm when one trolley of the fourth coach slipped off the tracks at a diamond crossing. Fortunately, no passengers were injured in the derailment. However, the incident disrupted train services, and railway authorities are working to restore operations. The Central Railways confirmed the derailment, stating that it occurred while the train was entering the Pune Station Platform. An investigation is likely to be conducted to determine the cause of the derailment. Railway officials are taking steps to resume normal train services as soon as possible. The derailment of the Vande Bharat Express has caused inconvenience to passengers, and efforts are being made to minimize the disruption.

stories.headline: Why the UAE asked Pakistan for its $3.5bn back
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has demanded immediate repayment of $3.5 billion from Pakistan, which is roughly one-fifth of Islamabad's central bank reserves. The request came as a surprise to Pakistan's economic managers and the International Monetary Fund (IMF), as Abu Dhabi had committed not to ask for the money before the end of Pakistan's $7 billion 2024 bailout programme in 2027. The $3.5 billion facility originated in 2018 and 2019, when the UAE placed deposits in the State Bank of Pakistan to prevent a reserve collapse. The repayment is expected to put pressure on Pakistan's reserves and may risk breaches of its IMF programme. Saudi Arabia has since stepped in with $3 billion to support Pakistan, as the country navigates its financial dependence and geopolitical relationships, including its attempts to mediate in the US, Israel, and Iran conflict.

stories.headline: Sterling edges up vs dollar with Middle East, BoE in focus
stories.summary: Sterling has edged up 0.08% against the US dollar, trading at $1.3544, as investors await key central bank meetings, including the Bank of England. The dollar had previously climbed due to the Middle East conflict, with investors seeking safe-haven assets. Against the euro, sterling fell 0.1% to 86.70 pence. European shares have also seen gains, with the UK's FTSE 100 up 0.81%, Germany's Dax up 0.46%, and France's CAC up 0.72%. The market is closely watching the situation in the Middle East, as well as upcoming central bank decisions, including the European Central Bank's rate decision. The Bank of England's meeting is also expected to impact sterling's value. Political developments in the UK, including Prime Minister Keir Starmer's appointment of Peter Mandelson as ambassador to the US, are also being monitored.

stories.headline: The Quiet Before the Storm: Geopolitics, Central Banks, and Earnings
stories.summary: Central banks are set to dominate the week with key announcements, starting with the Bank of Japan (BoJ) tomorrow, followed by the Bank of Canada (BoC) and Federal Reserve (Fed) on Wednesday. The BoJ is expected to hold its rate at 0.75%, with a mere 5% chance of a hike. Market attention will focus on signals from Governor Kazuo Ueda regarding future rate adjustments. Geopolitical risk, particularly the US-Iran situation, remains a dominant theme, capable of driving sudden market moves. Central banks are navigating a complicated inflation backdrop, with energy prices a key factor. The resilience of financial markets will be tested as central banks tighten policy to combat inflation, potentially exposing accumulated vulnerabilities. Earnings reports will also be closely watched, with weaker results potentially impacting equities amidst geopolitical uncertainty.

stories.headline: Markets have moved on from geopolitics, broader rally underway: Anurag Singh
stories.summary: Markets have largely absorbed geopolitical shocks, with the bottom seen at the end of March. According to Anurag Singh, the markets have moved on from the Iranian trouble, and a broader rally is underway. Recently, US equity markets fell sharply due to soaring oil prices and Middle East tensions, with the VIX reaching its highest level in a year. A $7-9 per barrel geopolitical risk premium was factored into oil prices. Trade policy shifts also impacted commodity markets and currency valuations, with oil prices and raw materials responding to the evolving trade landscape. Safe-haven assets like gold rallied amid heightened geopolitical risk perceptions, but markets have now shifted focus away from these concerns, indicating a potential recovery and upward trend. The current market sentiment suggests a move beyond the recent volatility.

stories.headline: As Kejriwal, Tejashwi rally behind Mamata, why Congress must read between the lines If Mamata Banerjee wins the Bengal polls, the INDIA bloc campaign, strikingly contrasting the Congress attack on her, could unveil a new Opposition power centre
stories.summary: Mamata Banerjee's TMC is receiving support from regional leaders in the West Bengal elections. Arvind Kejriwal, Tejashwi Yadav, Hemant Soren, and Akhilesh Yadav have campaigned for TMC candidates, aiming to curb the BJP's growth in the state. This alliance showcases opposition solidarity against the BJP. The Congress, however, is contesting separately. A win for Mamata Banerjee could unveil a new Opposition power centre, contrasting the Congress's attack on her. The INDIA bloc campaign has rallied behind Banerjee, with leaders like Vijay, Kejriwal, Soren, and Yadav showing support. The opposition's momentum hinges on TMC's performance in the elections. The alliance's success could potentially shift the opposition's power dynamics, with the TMC emerging as a key player.

stories.headline: Modi's BJP gains ground in India’s upper house after AAP lawmakers defect NEW DELHI, April 27 - Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s BJP party strengthened its position in parliament’s upper house after seven opposition lawmakers joi
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's BJP party has strengthened its position in parliament's upper house after seven opposition lawmakers joined it. A parliamentary list showed the shift on April 27, which could ease the government's passage of legislation. The seven lawmakers, from the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), defected to the BJP, boosting the party's numbers in the upper house. This development is expected to facilitate the government's ability to push through its legislative agenda. The BJP's increased strength in the upper house could lead to smoother passage of bills, as the party already holds a majority in the lower house of parliament. The shift in the upper house's composition may have significant implications for the government's policy initiatives and legislative priorities.

stories.headline: Modi's BJP gains ground in India's upper house after AAP lawmakers defect Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's BJP party strengthened its position in parliament's upper house after seven opposition lawmakers joined it, a parliamentar
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's BJP party has strengthened its position in parliament's upper house after seven opposition lawmakers from the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) defected to the BJP. The lawmakers, including Raghav Chadha, Sandeep Pathak, and Ashok Kumar Mittal, met with BJP president Nitin Nabin at the party's headquarters. The AAP has accused the BJP of running "Operation Lotus" to break and poach MPs. The defection bolsters the BJP's standing in the upper house of parliament. The move is seen as a calculated attempt to manipulate parliamentary strength, according to the Punjab Leader of Opposition. The development marks a significant gain for the BJP in the upper house, potentially altering the political landscape in India. The AAP has criticized the BJP's tactics, alleging a deliberate attempt to undermine opposition parties.

stories.headline: How Congress mouthpiece National Herald is peddling pro-Bangladeshi propaganda to discredit ECI and more On 26th April (Sunday), the Congress mouthpiece
stories.summary: The Congress mouthpiece National Herald published a column on April 26, suggesting the Modi government learn from Bangladesh's recent national parliament polls. The article is seen as an attempt to discredit the Election Commission of India (ECI). National Herald has previously published controversial opinion pieces, including one comparing the Ayodhya verdict to the Supreme Court of Pakistan. The outlet has also been involved in controversies surrounding the Rafale deal, with some arguing it inadvertently cried foul. National Herald's publications have been criticized for peddling pro-Bangladeshi propaganda and attempting to undermine Indian institutions. The outlet's articles have sparked debate and discussion, with some viewing them as an attempt to shape public opinion and influence political discourse. The Congress party's association with National Herald has also been subject to scrutiny.

stories.headline: Indian Equities Bounce Back: Sensex Jumps 639 Pts, Nifty Up 194 Pts
stories.summary: Indian equities rebounded, with the BSE Sensex jumping 639 points and the NSE Nifty climbing 194.75 points or 0.81% to close at 24,092.70. The market gains were driven by improved sentiment and expectations of de-escalation in the Middle East. Heavyweight stocks, including Sun Pharma and RIL, were top gainers, contributing to the strong momentum. The positive trend was also influenced by gains in global markets. The upswing comes ahead of the Economic Survey 2025, scheduled for January 31. The Nifty 50 rose 0.81%, reflecting the overall bullish sentiment in the Indian stock market. The Sensex and Nifty 50 indices closed higher, indicating a positive start to the week for Indian equities.

stories.headline: Sensex, Nifty Snap Losing Streak On Monday, End 0.8% Higher; Sun Pharma, IT Stocks Support Rally
stories.summary: India's benchmark indices, the Sensex and Nifty 50, ended 0.83% and 0.81% higher, respectively, on Monday, snapping a three-session losing streak. The Sensex closed at 77,303.63, up 639.42 points, while the Nifty closed at 24,092.70, gaining 194.75 points. This rebound was driven by gains in pharma and IT stocks, with Nifty Pharma rising 2.6% and Nifty Consumer Durables increasing 2.5%. Nifty Realty and Nifty Healthcare also jumped 2.4% each. The previous three sessions saw declines of 3.29% and 2.76% for the Sensex and Nifty, respectively. The market's bounce back on Monday was accompanied by easing volatility, despite crude oil prices remaining high. The Nifty 50 closed near the 24,100 mark, marking a positive start to the week.

stories.headline: Sensex, Nifty 50 snap 3-day losing run, end over 0.8% higher - 10 key highlights from the Indian stock market today
stories.summary: Benchmark equity indices in India snapped a three-day losing streak, rising by up to 0.83% on Monday. The Nifty 50 ended 0.8% higher, closing above the 24,000 mark at over 24,050. The BSE Sensex also gained, rising over 600 points. Buying emerged in beaten-down index heavyweights amid mixed global cues, despite uncertainty around stalled US-Iran talks. The pharma sector led the gains. Technically, the 50-day EMA in the 24,200-24,230 zone is expected to act as an immediate resistance for the Nifty 50. The market's upward movement halted a three-session decline, with the Nifty and Sensex breaking their losing streak. The gain was observed amid Iran's proposal to the US, contributing to the positive sentiment in the market. Overall, the Indian stock market ended the day on a positive note, with key indices recording significant gains.

stories.headline: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Tuesday
stories.summary: Stock markets are expected to be influenced by several factors on Tuesday. The index found resistance at the 38.20% Fibonacci retracement level of the previous fall, with potential resistance at 24,115-24,150. Previously, markets tumbled due to surging oil prices and foreign fund outflows. In international news, European stocks rose on Friday amid hopes of extra policy stimulus in China and ahead of key inflation readings. The pan-Eu STOXX 600 index increased, driven by expectations of interest rate guidance. Analysts, such as Rupak De of LKP Securities, are closely watching the market pulse to predict future movements. Key factors, including oil prices, foreign fund outflows, and inflation readings, will likely decide stock market action on Tuesday. Trading volume, intraday highs and lows, and day charts will also be closely monitored.

stories.headline: Hundreds of tech jobs at risk as Irish outsourcing firm Covalen informs workers of cuts to Meta work
stories.summary: Hundreds of tech jobs are at risk at Irish outsourcing firm Covalen due to cuts in its work with Meta. The company has commenced consultation with affected employees regarding potential job losses. Covalen's reliance on Meta as a primary client makes its workers vulnerable to changes in Meta's operations. Meta is currently undergoing significant restructuring, including cutting 14,000 jobs. Covalen has announced measures to support affected workers, including enhanced redundancy pay and retraining programs in AI-adjacent fields. The job cuts have been met with criticism over their timing, given the profitability of Covalen and Meta. The exact number of jobs at risk has not been disclosed, but workers have been left reeling by the announcement. Covalen is providing support to help workers transition into new roles. The consultation process is ongoing, with details of the job cuts expected to be finalized in the coming weeks.

stories.headline: Business confidence rising as lending rates drop - AGI CEO
stories.summary: Ghana's business confidence is rising due to a decline in lending rates, according to the Association of Ghana Industries (AGI) CEO, Seth Twum-Akwaboah. The private sector has shown strengthening business and investor confidence over the past six months, driven by emerging macroeconomic stability, consistent policy direction, and improved government-business dialogue. The Bank of Ghana's recent cuts in its policy rate, including a 350 basis points cut to 21.5% on September 18, 2025, are expected to trigger a new phase of lending and growth for businesses. This is the second cut in two months, following a 300 basis points cut earlier. The AGI CEO urges continued reforms to reduce production costs, enhance credit access, and support local industry for sustained growth and investment attraction. The decline in lending rates is seen as a key factor in boosting business confidence in Ghana's economy.

stories.headline: Concerns legal loophole is allowing landlords to run underground boarding houses
stories.summary: A legal loophole is allowing landlords to continue running underground boarding houses despite the federal eviction moratorium. The moratorium, intended to protect tenants during the pandemic, has a loophole that enables landlords to evict tenants. Landlords in gentrifying areas, such as Toronto, are taking advantage of this legislation to remove low-income tenants and raise rents without limit once a unit is vacant. They claim the process allows for necessary maintenance and argue that the focus should be on poverty reduction rather than rent control. The loophole is being exploited in various cities, including Omaha, where landlords are using it to evict tenants and increase rents. This has raised concerns among advocates, including the R.I. Center for Justice, which argues that the loophole undermines the purpose of the eviction moratorium.

stories.headline: KIRHub Opens A New Repurposing Map For Kinase Inhibitors In Lung Cancer
stories.summary: KIRHub has launched a new repurposing map for kinase inhibitors in lung cancer, focusing on approved kinase drugs across various variants, including EGFR, ALK, RET, and MET. The MAP Kinase (MAPK) signalling pathway is highlighted, explaining how it goes wrong in cancer. Research shows that certain kinase inhibitors, such as SBI-0206965, can induce apoptosis and autophagy inhibition in lung cancer cells. Additionally, fenbendazole, a low-cost and safe benzimidazole compound, has shown unique anti-proliferative activities, making it a potential candidate for cancer treatment. The repurposing of fenbendazole is being explored, with emphasis on ensuring patient safety. The KIRHub map aims to facilitate the discovery of new therapeutic uses for existing kinase inhibitors in lung cancer. This initiative may lead to more effective and targeted treatments for lung cancer patients.

stories.headline: AI Funding Surges Led by Frontier Models In 2026, artificial intelligence (AI) funding maintained strong momentum, with volumes surging and major technology firms acquiring AI capabilities at an early
stories.summary: Artificial intelligence funding surged in 2026, with volumes increasing significantly. According to the Q1 2026 State of AI report by CB Insights, major technology firms are acquiring AI capabilities at an early stage. The AI funding boom is driven by rapid advancements in generative AI technologies, including large language models and text-to-image models. A record-breaking $300 billion in AI-focused venture capital reflects strong investor confidence in the transformative potential of artificial intelligence. This surge is accelerating AI development and creating innovative solutions across multiple sectors. The growth of AI funding represents both opportunity and risk for the technology industry, with increased attention from practitioners, industry leaders, policymakers, and the general public. The AI Index Report highlights the significance of AI in global discourse, with news coverage focusing on AI technologies, companies, and ethical issues.

stories.headline: OpenAI breaks free from exclusive AI pact with Microsoft The new pact is meant to simplify a complicated relationship that has been foundational to OpenAI’s rise and the broader artificial intelligence boom.
stories.summary: OpenAI has ended its exclusive artificial intelligence pact with Microsoft, simplifying their complicated relationship. The new agreement allows OpenAI to sell its products, including ChatGPT, across rival cloud platforms. Microsoft will no longer have exclusive access to OpenAI's technology, clearing the way for OpenAI's models to appear on Amazon Web Services and other cloud-computing providers. Although Azure will remain OpenAI's primary cloud provider, the company will now operate under a multi-cloud model. This change marks a significant shift in one of the most consequential alliances in the artificial intelligence era, enabling OpenAI to expand its reach and presence in the market. The revised partnership takes effect immediately, with OpenAI poised to explore new opportunities and collaborations with other cloud providers. Azure's primary status is maintained, but OpenAI's growth is no longer limited by exclusivity.

stories.headline: Elon Musk sues OpenAI as diary surfaces in court The bitter legal fight between Elon Musk and the leading artificial intelligence firm may come down to a few pages in one executive's personal notes.
stories.summary: Elon Musk has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, its CEO Sam Altman, and former CEO Greg Brockman, alleging breach of contract. The lawsuit seeks to force OpenAI to revert to its original principles, which Musk claims were agreed upon when he co-founded the company in 2015. Musk was an early backer of OpenAI, but disagreements arose in 2017 over commercializing the company. The lawsuit has brought to light a personal diary belonging to an executive, which may hold significant evidence. Musk claims OpenAI has strayed from its original mission, prompting the legal action. The case marks a significant escalation in the rift between Musk and OpenAI's leadership, with the company's direction and future at stake. The lawsuit highlights the tension between Musk's vision for OpenAI and the company's current trajectory.

stories.headline: OpenAI Publishes 5 Principles For Its AGI Push Sam Altman published five principles for OpenAI's work toward artificial general intelligence. The company wants broad access but reserves room to restrict capa
stories.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has published five principles guiding the company's work toward artificial general intelligence (AGI). The principles aim to ensure AGI benefits all of humanity, focusing on broad access while reserving the right to restrict capabilities. The five principles are: democratization, empowerment, universal prosperity, resilience, and adaptability. These principles will guide OpenAI's internal decision-making and strategic direction as it navigates advanced AI research and deployment. The framework prioritizes making AI accessible to many, empowering individuals, and fostering universal prosperity, while also building resilience against risks and maintaining adaptability as the technology evolves. This marks OpenAI's first major rewrite of its guiding document since its 2018 charter.
